newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks rise gently in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks rise gently in low volume.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose gently in low volume, reversing some of last week's losses but failing to establish a definite new upwards trend, traders said.
"Trade has been light becuase we've had neither good or bad news ... the market's waiting a clearer outcome of the labor reform talks," said one trader.
The bolsa's 19-share rose 0.71 percent to close at 6,177.68 points as 23 million shares traded, worth 2.5 billion bolivars ($5.2 million).
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, rose 1.1 percent to close at 95.16 points.

Venezuelan equities, which soared over 100 percent in 1996, are down over eight percent this year -- the worst performing market in the region. "We believe the market has not entirely factored in significant advances such as the tripartite commission's agreement to reform the severance benefits system, the reduction in inflation and the sincere efforts of the executive ... to continue the privatization of steel and aluminum companies," said Santander Investment.
Santander added it expected the market to move again when the labor reforms passed Congress and the index to register a 32 percent gain in dollar terms by the end of the year.
